newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent extends rally on renewed Iraq tension.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent extends rally on renewed Iraq tension.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures extended their rally after the NYMEX open on Wednesday, as renewed tension in Iraq kept the fire under the market burning.
October Brent touched a new post-Gulf War high of $23.65 per barrel before edging down to $23.59 by 1428 GMT, still 71 cents above Tuesday's close.

Iraq fired missiles at U.S. jets over northern Iraq on Wednesday but missed their targets, and the U.S. moved B-52 bombers to a base in the Indian Ocean to back its threat of new military strikes on Iraq, U.S. defence officials said.
"The rally is mainly emotional," a broker said.

"The Iraqi news was just a catalyst for an already strong market," said another, citing the latest U.S. API oil inventory data which showed falling crude and gasoline stocks, and a continuing year-on-year shortfall in distillates.
"The APIs were good, technically it's strong and heating oil is tight," he added.
However, wet crude traders said the Atlantic basin crude market was oversupplied.
IPE gas oil kept up well with crude, hovering just below a five-year spot month high of $226.25 per tonne. By 1502 GMT, September futures stood $6.00 higher at $224.00.
The October Brent/gas oil crack spread traded at $5.60 per barrel on Wednesday, 20 cents off its recent high, but still far above its recent low of $4.15 on August 19.
